payload.title: AI Builders Daily · 2026-06-13
payload.summary:
**Anthropic** spent the day cleaning house: a blunt **Claude Code** postmortem, a bigger **Managed Agents** architecture reveal, and a new push into self-hosted sandboxes plus private **MCP** tunnels; **Fable** turned into the flashpoint, with builders debating access shutdowns, ID checks, and whether governments are starting to regulate models instead of uses; **Vercel** pushed **HarnessAgent** to break agent lock-in while the podcast circuit kept hammering the same thesis: coding agents are stretching into longer horizons and open-weight economics look shakier; meanwhile **SpaceX** stole the emotional oxygen, pulling awe-struck reactions from half the timeline.

**Anthropic** 今天连发几枪：先把 **Claude Code** 近期变差的锅摊开讲明白，又把 **Managed Agents** 的底层设计掰开了讲，顺手还把自托管沙箱和私有 **MCP** 通道推上台面；另一边 **Fable** 直接炸场，停用、限人、实名门槛这些话题全冒出来了，讨论已经不是产品体验，而是模型到底该不该被管；**Vercel** 也没闲着，扔出 **HarnessAgent** 去拆代理锁定，播客圈则在反复确认一件事：代码代理开始真干长活了，但开源权重这门生意看着越来越悬；至于情绪面，今天基本被 **SpaceX** 一把拿走。

sections.headline: Coding agents grow up, and open-weight optimism fades / 代码代理开始扛长活，开源权重的乐观情绪在降温
sections.body:
This episode’s big takeaway is that coding agents are no longer just cute copilots. Ari from **Datalogy** says teams are starting to manage swarms of agents over longer time horizons, shifting engineers toward agent supervision while creating new review and comprehension bottlenecks. The panel also argues that compute pressure and weak business models are pushing frontier labs away from open-weight releases, with smaller cheaper models gaining appeal mostly because enterprise bills are suddenly painful.

这一期最硬的点有两个。第一，代码代理已经不只是补全工具了，**Datalogy** 的 Ari 说很多团队开始真的在管一群代理，工程师更像调度员，但新问题也来了：代码暴涨，审查和理解反而成了卡点。第二，几位嘉宾明显对开源权重没那么乐观了，算力紧、账单高、商业模式又站不稳，前沿实验室更可能把最强模型关进 API；便宜小模型之所以重新吃香，不是情怀回归，是企业真被费用打疼了。

sections.headline: **Anthropic** explains the **Claude Code** regression mess / **Anthropic** 解释了 **Claude Code** 近期变差到底怎么回事
sections.body:
**Anthropic** says the **Claude API** itself was fine; the regressions came from product-layer changes around **Claude Code**, the Agent SDK, and Cowork. The post names three causes: lowering default reasoning effort to cut latency, a caching bug that kept dropping prior reasoning after idle sessions, and a prompt tweak meant to reduce verbosity that hurt coding quality. All three were rolled back or fixed by April 20, and the company says it is tightening review and testing around these harness-level changes.

**Anthropic** 的说法很直接：出问题的不是 **Claude API** 本身，而是 **Claude Code** 这一层自己动了几刀，结果刀刀见血。具体三件事，一是把默认思考强度调低来换速度，结果用户觉得模型变钝了；二是缓存优化写崩了，闲置会话恢复后会不断丢掉之前的推理，表现出来就是健忘、重复、工具乱用；三是为了少说废话加了提示词，最后把写代码能力也一块削了。现在这些改动都撤了或修了，这篇基本就是一次公开认错。

sections.headline: **Managed Agents** splits the brain, the hands, and the session / **Managed Agents** 把“大脑”“手脚”“会话”彻底拆开
sections.body:
**Anthropic** frames **Managed Agents** as a durable interface layer for long-running agents. The key design move is to decouple the model harness from the sandbox and from the session log, so each can fail, restart, or be swapped independently. That makes sandboxes disposable instead of precious, improves recovery after crashes, and keeps credentials away from untrusted generated code by pushing auth into vaults and proxies rather than the execution environment.

这篇不是产品稿，味道更像架构复盘。**Anthropic** 的核心判断是，长时代理不能再把所有东西塞进一个容器里养成“宠物机”。所以它把代理的大脑、动手的沙箱、还有事件会话日志硬拆开：沙箱挂了就重建，编排器挂了就按会话日志续上，凭证也别进沙箱，直接放到金库和代理层后面。好处很实在，系统更扛摔，调试更清楚，安全边界也总算像回事了。

sections.headline: **Claude Managed Agents** adds self-hosted sandboxes and private **MCP** tunnels / **Claude Managed Agents** 新增自托管沙箱和私有 **MCP** 通道
sections.body:
The update pushes **Managed Agents** deeper into enterprise infrastructure. Tool execution can now run inside a customer-controlled sandbox or through providers like **Cloudflare**, **Daytona**, **Modal**, and **Vercel**, while Anthropic still handles orchestration. The second addition is **MCP** tunnels, which let agents call private internal tools through a single outbound encrypted connection instead of exposing those services on the public internet.

这次更新瞄得很准，就是往企业内网里钻。现在代理真正干活的那层可以放进你自己的沙箱里，也可以挂到 **Cloudflare**、**Daytona**、**Modal**、**Vercel** 这些托管环境上，Anthropic 留在外面做编排。另一个更关键的点是私有 **MCP** 通道：内部数据库、私有 API、知识库这些东西，不用暴露公网，也能给代理调起来。对大公司来说，这比“更聪明一点”重要得多。

sections.headline: Maybe the future codebase kills **Git** / 也许未来的代码库该把 **Git** 一起送走
sections.body:
## The Future Codebase

After the PR dies, after the Code Review dies,
i am seriously wondering if Git needs to die next.

roughly 20-40% of code spend is just managing and updating merge conflicts. necessary evil? or legacy "horseless carriage"? cargo culting the past?

we don't do line by line merge conflicts when we collaborate with human colleagues - instead we chat, suggest edits, do side comments, and an owner ships it. 

btw we also don't do CI/CD even collaborating on documents with serious legal/financial implications.

maybe the future codebase looks more like a Notion or Linear database than .git objects. It will be less efficient, but more scalable. exactly the Salty Lesson.

## 未来的代码库

等 PR 死了，等 Code Review 死了，
我现在真的开始怀疑，下一个该死的是不是 **Git**。

大概 20% 到 40% 的代码成本，都花在处理和更新合并冲突上。它到底是必要之恶，还是“无马马车”式的历史包袱？只是对过去的盲目模仿？

我们跟同事协作时，并不会逐行解决合并冲突。我们会聊天、提修改建议、留边注，然后由负责人发版。

顺便说一句，我们在协作文档时也不会搞 CI/CD，哪怕那些文档牵涉严肃的法律或财务问题。

未来的代码库也许更像 **Notion** 或 **Linear** 里的数据库，而不是 `.git` 对象。它可能没那么高效，但更能扩展。很像那个 **Salty Lesson**。

sections.headline: Levie says model-level regulation just crossed a line / Levie 认为监管已经开始直接碰模型本身了
sections.body:
This is a big turning point for AI regulation.

The government is starting to deem some models too powerful for certain uses, which creates a precedent for a range of possible controls in the future.

I’m in the camp that this is unnecessary and we should be primarily regulating the use of AI, as opposed to the underlying models. But, equally, there are plenty of people that actually prefer this outcome.

Either way, it’s unlikely that we’re going back to a world where the government doesn’t have far more meaningful involvement in the rate of AI progress.

这对 AI 监管来说是个很大的转折点。

政府已经开始认定某些模型强到不该用于某些场景，这会为未来一整套可能的控制手段开先例。

我个人觉得这没必要，监管重点应该放在 AI 的使用方式，而不是底层模型本身。当然，也确实有不少人更喜欢这种结果。

但不管你站哪边，那个“政府不会更深介入 AI 进展速度”的世界，大概率回不去了。

sections.headline: AI coding can scaffold bureaucracy just as fast / AI 编程工具不只会加速创造，也会加速官僚化
sections.body:
Everyone thinks AI coding tools set founders free.

Watch what people actually build with them: rules, approvals, process, layers. The same cage, assembled faster.

The tool that can scaffold anything in an afternoon will scaffold your bureaucracy in an afternoon too.

Speed of construction is speed of calcification. Build the thing that lets you create new things: experiences that didn’t happen before.

大家都觉得 AI 编程工具能把创始人解放出来。

但你看看大家实际拿它做了什么：规则、审批、流程、层层套娃。同一个笼子，只是搭得更快。

一个下午能把任何东西 scaffold 出来的工具，也能在一个下午把你的官僚体系 scaffold 出来。

建得越快，固化得也越快。去做那种能让你创造新东西的东西，做以前根本没出现过的体验。

sections.headline: Builder overload is turning attention into the real bottleneck / 构建者太多了，真正稀缺的是注意力
sections.body:
There are SO many people, friends, acquaintances, followers, startups, asking me to try their new AI products every day

Like I get at least 3 such requests per day

If I tried all of these products I wouldn’t have time to do anything else 

There are too many builders and the competition for attention is insane

每天都有一堆人来找我试他们新的 AI 产品，朋友、熟人、关注者、创业公司，全都有。

这种请求我一天至少收到 3 个。

sections.headline: Two voices, one person / 一个人，偏偏有两种说话声线
sections.body:
Anyone else have two voices?

I often have two voices that come out both in my writing and how I speak. 

One is the frenetic, time is the enemy, direct, punchy gets to the point quickly and then the second is more calm, measured, structured inquisitive, trying to peel the layers. 

They are distinctive enough that people think it’s two different people (especially in writing). 

They are usually separate but I feel I often oscillate between the two in the same conversation.

还有别人也会有两种声音吗？

我在写东西和说话时，经常会冒出两种不同的声线。

一种很躁，觉得时间是敌人，直接、短促、很快切到重点；另一种则更平静、更克制、更有结构，带点追问，想把一层层东西剥开。

它们差别大到别人会以为是两个人写的，尤其是在文字里。

通常这两种状态是分开的，但我感觉自己也常常会在同一段对话里来回切。

Codex runs INSIDE crabbox while it is building crabbox.
This is becoming essential infra for my work.

Codex been looping nonstop for the last 4 days in multiple trees. Since all of it is e2e verifiable it basically builds itself. Codex even signs up for the services automatically via browser/computer use. My main job is adding credit card details and closing things that I don't see as a fit.

**Codex** 现在直接跑在 crabbox 里面，一边构建 crabbox 一边继续干活。
这已经快成我工作的核心基础设施了。

**Codex** 过去 4 天在多个代码树里几乎没停过，因为整套东西都能做端到端验证，所以它基本是在自己搭自己。它甚至会通过 browser/computer use 自动注册服务。我的主要工作反而变成填信用卡信息，以及关掉那些我觉得不合适的东西。
